summary: All 8 frames were reached and captured (recipe now written to .vicifull/recipes/handover.json plus .vicifull/drives/handover-walk.js — the previous agent left none). Sigs: v-handover-d-* vs v-handover-a-*. Geometry, type and copy are in fact very good: Reminders Setup is 0 differing / 0 missing, The Vow and Medallion Received differ only in radius notation, and Letter Week XII's margin-collapse fixes are correct (26 / 56 / 36 all land). But the report's single biggest "could not match" claim is false, and it hides five real, currently-visible defects. The claim that a RadialGradient's radius "cannot reach the DOM through the public component" is wrong: on web `RadialGradient` is elements.web.js's WebShape (tag `radialGradient`) and `prepare()` forwards props verbatim, so `r` DOES reach the DOM — I read the live DOM and it shows `<radialGradient cx="38%" cy="30%" rx="93.5%" ry="93.5%">` with no `r`. This is already a recorded project decision (D064) and is already applied to the IDENTICAL art in two sibling files the same agent had open: src/app/letter.tsx:419 (WaxSeal) and src/app/medallion-post.tsx:177 (md-face), and src/app/vow.tsx:86-93 carries the explanation verbatim. So all three farthest-corner gradients in handover.tsx (letSeal, vowSun, medFace) render 50%-radius and measurably too dark — up to 53 alpha-units off. Those same two sibling files also re-paint the disc's inset rim light with `insetOf()` because an absolutely-positioned <Svg> face covers the parent View's inset box-shadow; handover.tsx does not, so the wax seal's and the medallion's white rims are simply not drawn — plainly visible in a 3x/6x crop. Separately, the three Campaign Map frames draw their paper grain through art.tsx's local `Noise` (expo-image contentFit="cover"), which magnifies the 96x96 tile ~8.9x into a smear — the exact failure src/components/ui/Grain.tsx documents and avoids; the signature diff is clean while the texture is visibly wrong, which is this project's known failure mode. Finally I confirmed the report's textWrap observation is a real, visible line-break mismatch on both Reminders notification bodies, and that src/app/vow.tsx:26 already establishes the local workaround the agent chose not to apply.

findings.element: the wax seal, 48x48 disc at left 106 / top 112 inside the 260x260 art frame
findings.design: farthest-corner = 93.5% of the box; measured upper-left 238,216,177 and right rim 227,189,125
findings.app: handover.tsx:200 `<RadialGradient id="letSeal" cx="38%" cy="30%" rx="93.5%" ry="93.5%">` with no `r`, so the browser falls back to r=50%; measured 227,189,126 (Δ51) and 201,159,95 (Δ30)
findings.note: NOT one of the two known equivalences. The report calls this unverifiable and unfixable; that is wrong. On web react-native-svg resolves RadialGradient from elements.web.js (a WebShape with tag 'radialGradient') and `prepare()` copies unknown props straight onto the DOM node — I read the live app DOM and it is `<radialGradient cx="38%" cy="30%" rx="93.5%" ry="93.5%">`. Adding `r="93.5%"` fixes web and is inert on native (elements/RadialGradient.js does `rx: rx || r`). This is already DECISIONS D064, and src/app/letter.tsx:419 draws this exact seal with `r="93.5%" rx="93.5%" ry="93.5%"` and the comment explaining why.

findings.design: a pale 3px ring visible all the way round the seal (clear at 6x crop)
findings.app: not drawn at all — handover.tsx:188 puts the inset shadow on the wrapper View and then paints the gradient with an absolutely-positioned `<Svg>` child, which CSS paints above the parent's inset shadow
findings.note: src/app/letter.tsx solves precisely this: `insetOf(shadow)` lifts the inset segments out and re-paints them on an overlay View above the art (letter.tsx:399-431), with a comment stating the rule. handover.tsx's own engraved-ring View (line 452) is drawn as such an overlay and IS visible, which is the control that proves the mechanism.

findings.element: the 136pt medallion face at left 62 / top 52
findings.app: handover.tsx:444 `medFace` states only rx/ry 93.5%, so web renders r=50%; measured 201,159,95 (Δ53), 201,159,95 (Δ26), 229,194,135 (Δ21)
findings.note: Same D064 violation. src/app/medallion-post.tsx:177 draws the same disc with `r="93.5%" rx="93.5%" ry="93.5%"` and names D064 in its comment.

findings.element: the medallion disc's rim light and warm floor
findings.design: a pale 4px ring outside the engraved circle and a soft warm darkening along the bottom inner edge — both obvious at 3x
findings.app: neither is drawn; handover.tsx:433 puts both insets on the parent View and the face `<Svg>` (line 441, position absolute) paints over them
findings.note: medallion-post.tsx:181 fixes the identical disc with `<View ... boxShadow={insetOf(DISC_SHADOW)} />` above the face. Together with the radius defect this is why the app's coin reads as a flat darker ball rather than a lit struck disc.

findings.app: handover.tsx:355 `vowSun` states only rx/ry 79.7%, web renders r=50%; measured 227,190,133 (Δ32), 235,204,152 (Δ21), 245,231,207 (Δ15) — a visible dark ring at the rim
findings.note: Same D064 violation. src/app/vow.tsx:86-97 — a file in this same group — already writes its two gradients with `r` and `gradientUnits="userSpaceOnUse"` and carries the comment 'on web prepare() forwards props straight to the DOM, and rx/ry are not <radialGradient> attributes'. The agent had the answer in the file next door.

findings.frame: #40 Campaign Map / #41 Campaign Map II / #42 Campaign Map III
findings.element: the full-frame paper grain over the map field
findings.property: background-image: url('noise-dark.png') with no background-size → tiles at the file's own 96x96; opacity 0.12
findings.design: fine even speckle; sign-changes per row in a flat band (frame y648-688) = 148, sd 1.34
findings.app: a ~8.9x magnified smear — large soft blotches; flips/row = 62 at the same amplitude (sd 1.26). CampaignMapField (art.tsx:1026) uses art.tsx's local `Noise` (line 54), an expo-image with `contentFit="cover"`, so one 96x96 tile is stretched to 393x852. Confirmed in the live DOM: `` natural 96x96, computed object-fit cover, 393px x 852px.
findings.note: src/components/ui/Grain.tsx exists specifically to avoid this and says so in its header ('expo-image has no repeat mode — its contentFit="cover" blows one tile up to fill the box, roughly a 9x magnification, and turns the grain into a smear'); it uses RN Image resizeMode="repeat", which does work on web — the letter and medallion frames, which use Grain, measure 118 vs 116 flips/row against their designs. Signature-invisible, PNG-obvious: exactly the failure mode the brief warns about. The file is art.tsx (GROUP funnel's), but these three frames are where it shows; `Noise` is also used at art.tsx:168/323/336/384, so other groups are affected.

findings.element: both notification card bodies — 'Twenty seconds — where's your head at today?' and 'The time you told us about. SOS is one tap away.'
findings.design: the canvas sets no `text-wrap` on these runs; they break '…where's your head at / today?' and '…SOS is one tap / away.'
findings.app: '…where's your head / at today?' and '…SOS is one / tap away.' — src/components/ui/AppText.tsx:128 forces `textWrap: 'pretty'` on web for every non-hero/display/title variant
findings.note: Confirmed by 2x crops of both cards. The signature diff is clean (0 differing, 0 missing) because the line count and the 309pt box are unchanged — a screenshot was needed. The report flagged this but left it; src/app/vow.tsx:26 already establishes the local fix (a Platform.OS === 'web' textWrap override on the one run whose canvas value differs), so a per-run override on these two bodies is available without touching the shared file. The report's claim that device rendering is unaffected is plausible (RN ignores textWrap) but I could not verify it on device.

findings.element: the report's 'Could not match' section, first bullet
findings.property: factual correctness of a blocking claim
findings.app: 'Neither rx, ry nor r can reach the DOM through the public component (RadialGradient.render forwards only rx/ry, and extractGradient drops the rest). So the three farthest-corner fixes above are correct on device and inert in the web preview.'
findings.note: False, and it is the reason five of the defects above are still live. lib/module/elements/RadialGradient.js is the NATIVE component; metro resolves lib/module/ReactNativeSVG.web.js → elements.web.js for web, where RadialGradient is `class RadialGradient extends WebShape { tag = 'radialGradient' }` and web/utils/prepare.js spreads `...rest` onto the element. `r` therefore reaches the DOM on web, and native honours `rx || r`, so stating all three is right on both — which is exactly what DECISIONS D064 already rules ('worth sweeping across every other screen that draws a farthest-corner radial') and what letter.tsx, medallion-post.tsx and vow.tsx already do. Also note art.tsx:512 (SunDisc, called at art.tsx:457 with r="93.5%") has the same unswept defect, outside this group.
